### 1.  Discriminant of \(f\)

For a cubic \(ax^{3}+bx^{2}+cx+d\),

\[
\Delta = 18abcd-4b^{3}d+b^{2}c^{2}-4ac^{3}-27a^{2}d^{2}.
\]

Here \(a=1,\;b=1,\;c=q,\;d=9\). Hence

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta
&=18(1)(1)(q)(9)-4(1)^{3}(9)+(1)^{2}q^{2}-4(1)q^{3}-27(1)^{2}9^{2}\\[2mm]
&=162q-36+q^{2}-4q^{3}-2187\\[2mm]
&=-4q^{3}+q^{2}+162q-2223.
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 2.  Factoring \(\Delta\)

Solve \(\Delta=0\):

\[
-4q^{3}+q^{2}+162q-2223=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
4q^{3}-q^{2}-162q+2223=0.
\]

A rational root is \(q=-\dfrac{39}{4}\) (check: \(-4(-39/4)^{3}+(-39/4)^{2}+162(-39/4)-2223=0\)).

\[

\]

\]

The quadratic factor satisfies  

\[
q^{2}-10q+57=(q-5)^{2}+32>0\qquad(\forall q\in\mathbb R).
\]

Hence the sign of \(\Delta\) is the opposite of the sign of \(4q+39\):

\[
\Delta<0 \iff 4q+39>0 \iff q>-\frac{39}{4}.
\]

- \(\Delta>0\) ⇒ the cubic has three distinct real roots.
- \(\Delta=0\) ⇒ a multiple real root (two distinct real roots, one repeated).

Therefore, for every \(q\) larger than the value where \(\Delta\) changes sign, the polynomial possesses exactly one real zero.
